name: sim_weyl_chirality_g_reduction_noncomm
scope_note: Non-commutativity: Weyl L-projector before vs after SU(2)->SO(3) G-tower step yields distinct surviving state families. PATH A (L then SU->SO) spans grade-0+grade-2 [irreps 0e+1e]; PATH B (SU->SO then L) spans grade-0 only [irrep 0e]. z3 UNSAT proves structural impossibility of equality. Ref: ENGINE_MATH_REFERENCE.md; LADDERS_FENCES_ADMISSION_REFERENCE.md.

pyg.reason: no graph learning required; probe operates on density matrices not graph structures

z3.reason: UNSAT guard: proves no assignment of rotor and spinor params makes P_L-before and P_L-after yield identical outputs under non-trivial conditions

cvc5.reason: z3 sufficient for all separability and product-form UNSAT proofs in this sim

geomstats.reason: no Riemannian manifold computation required; geometry handled analytically

e3nn.reason: SO(3) irrep decomposition and parity labeling of surviving state families: grade-0 ~ irrep 0e, grade-2 bivectors ~ irrep 1e; confirms families live in distinct SO(3) representations

rustworkx.reason: no graph traversal or path computation required in this probe

xgi.reason: no hypergraph structure required; probe uses standard matrix operations

toponetx.reason: no chain complex or cell complex computation required in this probe

noncommutativity_generic_spinor.note: PATH A output has grade-2 component; PATH B output is pure grade-0

family_A_spans_grade0_and_grade2.note: PATH A family lives in grade-0 PLUS grade-2 subspace after SU(2) action

family_B_spans_grade0_only.note: PATH B family is confined to grade-0 (scalar) subspace only

families_are_distinguishably_different.note: surviving state families differ: PATH A has 0e+1e irreps, PATH B has 0e only

R_and_negR_give_same_SO3_on_vectors.note: confirms SU(2) double cover: R and -R same sandwich product

R_and_negR_distinct_on_spinors.note: R and -R give DIFFERENT left actions on spinors, confirming double cover

z3_unsat_generic_ordering_equality.note: UNSAT: no assignment of (a0!=0, a2!=0, b!=0, unit rotor) makes P_L-before == P_L-after; proves orderings structurally distinct

z3_unsat_pure_L_spinor_grade2_noncomm.note: UNSAT even for pure L spinor: PATH A produces grade-2 output; PATH B produces zero grade-2; cannot be equal with b!=0 and a0!=0

identity_rotor_paths_agree.note: theta=0: R=identity so both orderings trivially agree (no rotation applied)

pure_R_spinor_paths_differ.note: pure R-type spinor: PATH A kills signal (P_L(s)=0 then rotate=0), PATH B leaks grade-2 into grade-0 via rotation (b*a2 term)

half_rotation_paths_differ.note: theta=pi: R=e12; PATH A output is pure e12 (grade-2); PATH B output is grade-0 scalar; clearly distinct

e3nn_irrep_families_distinct.note: family A (L-before) spans 0e+1e irreps; family B (L-after) spans 0e only; different SO(3) irrep content confirms distinguishable state families

grade2_bivectors_are_1e_irrep.note: Cl(3) grade-2 bivectors (e12,e13,e23) transform as SO(3) 1e (axial/pseudovector, even parity) — confirms irrep assignment

z3_boundary_zero_L_component_still_unsat.note: boundary: even with a0=0, P_L-before gives 0 but P_L-after gives -b*a2 (nonzero); z3 UNSAT confirms cannot be equal
